```{python setup}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

import os
import sys
import math

sys.path.append('.')

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Polygon as MplPolygon, Rectangle, Ellipse

from notes_style import (use_chapter, save, tidy, dim_x,
                         INK, LOADCLR, REACTCLR, DIMCLR,
                         DOMCLR, BDRYCLR, FLUXCLR)

IMGDIR = use_chapter("Poisson1D_Rod")

# ---- the worked example used throughout this page (SI units) ---------------
# An end-bearing concrete pile: loaded at its head, resisted along its shaft by
# skin friction, and seated on rock at its toe.  x runs DOWN the pile.
L    = 10.0          # m    pile length
E    = 30.0e9        # Pa   concrete
A    = 0.30 * 0.30   # m^2  square pile, 300 mm x 300 mm
EA   = E * A         # N
P    = 900.0e3       # N    column load on the head, pointing down (+x)
fsk  = -40.0e3       # N/m  skin friction, pointing up (-x)
ROD  = "#e2e2e2"     # the rod's body
SOIL = "#efe3cf"
ROCK = "#c9c3b8"


def arrow(ax, p_from, p_to, color=INK, lw=1.8, ms=13, z=6, style="-|>"):
    ax.annotate("", xy=p_to, xytext=p_from,
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle=style, color=color, lw=lw,
                                mutation_scale=ms, shrinkA=0, shrinkB=0),
                zorder=z)


def graph(ax, xlabel=None, ylabel=None):
    """A plotted function: left and bottom axes only."""
    for s in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
    for s in ("left", "bottom"):
        ax.spines[s].set_linewidth(0.9)
    if xlabel:
        ax.set_xlabel(xlabel, fontsize=11)
    if ylabel:
        ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, fontsize=11)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=9.5)


def box(ax, x0, x1, y0, y1, fc=ROD, ec=INK, lw=1.3, z=1, alpha=1.0, **kw):
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((min(x0, x1), min(y0, y1)), abs(x1 - x0),
                           abs(y1 - y0), facecolor=fc, edgecolor=ec, lw=lw,
                           zorder=z, alpha=alpha, **kw))


def hatch_wall(ax, x, y0, y1, side=1, n=7, size=0.28, color=INK, lw=1.3):
    """A fixed support: a solid line with hatching on one side."""
    ax.plot([x, x], [y0, y1], color=color, lw=lw * 1.4, zorder=6)
    for yv in np.linspace(y0, y1, n):
        ax.plot([x, x + side * size], [yv, yv - size], color=color, lw=lw,
                zorder=6)


def axial_arrows(ax, x0, x1, y, sign, n=7, size=0.45, color=LOADCLR, lw=1.3,
                 scale=None):
    """Small arrows along a bar showing a distributed axial load f.
    `scale(x)` in [0, 1] optionally sizes each arrow by the local |f|."""
    for xv in np.linspace(x0, x1, n + 2)[1:-1]:
        s = size * (scale(xv) if scale else 1.0)
        if s < 0.04:
            continue
        arrow(ax, (xv - sign * s / 2, y), (xv + sign * s / 2, y), color=color,
              lw=lw, ms=9)
```

This page is the companion to [1D Poisson I: Heat Conduction Through a Wall](Poisson1D_Heat.qmd).
Both read Hughes' one-dimensional model problem,

::: {.derivation}
$$
(\mathrm{S}) \qquad
\begin{aligned}
&\text{Given } f : \bar\Omega \to \RR \text{ and constants } g \text{ and } h,
 \text{ find } u : \bar\Omega \to \RR \text{ such that} \\[2pt]
&\qquad u_{,xx} + f = 0 \quad \text{on } \Omega = \,]0,1[ \\
&\qquad u(1) = g \\
&\qquad -u_{,x}(0) = h
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

or, with the length and the material constant put back, as in [Class 4](4_Class.qmd),

::: {.derivation}
$$
-\left(K u_{,x}\right)_{,x} = f \quad \text{in } \Omega = \,]0, L[
\qquad\qquad
u = g \quad \text{on } \Gamma_g
\qquad\qquad
\left(K u_{,x}\right) n = h \quad \text{on } \Gamma_h
$$
:::

On this page $u$ is an **axial displacement** and $K = EA$ is the **axial stiffness**.
The equations are letter-for-letter those of the wall. The difference is in what $h$
*means*, and it changes the sign of $h$ in a way that trips people up; see
[the boundary conditions](#sec-rod-neumann) below.

## The physical problem

![A concrete pile carrying a column load to rock. The load comes in at the head, part of
it is shed into the soil along the shaft by friction, and the rest is delivered to the rock
at the toe. On the right, the same pile as a one-dimensional model.](`{python} fig_pile_path`){#fig-r-pile width=98%}

The pile is long and slender, and the loads act along its axis, so the only motion that
matters is along the axis. Every cross-section at depth $x$ moves the same distance
$u(x)$ down the pile: one number per cross-section, a function of one variable.

| What happens physically | Where | Becomes |
|---|---|---|
| Soil grips the shaft and resists its downward motion | throughout $\Omega$ | the forcing $f$ |
| The toe sits on rock that does not move | $x = L$ | a Dirichlet condition $u = g = 0$ |
| The column pushes down on the head with a known force | $x = 0$ | a Neumann condition $(EA\,u_{,x})\,n = h$ |

Nothing about the equation cares that the pile is vertical. $x$ can point any way, as
long as every sign is read relative to it. Here $+x$ is **down**.

## The one-dimensional domain

```{python fig_domain}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.4, 2.3))
Ld = 6.0
box(ax, 0, Ld, -0.18, 0.18, fc=ROD, ec=INK)
ax.text(Ld / 2, 0.36, r"$\Omega$", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=17)
for xv, n, lab in ((0.0, -1, "$x=0$"), (Ld, 1, "$x=L$")):
    ax.plot([xv], [0], "o", color=INK, ms=8, zorder=6)
    ax.text(xv, -0.4, lab, ha="center", va="top", fontsize=11.5)
    arrow(ax, (xv, 0), (xv + 1.1 * n, 0), color=REACTCLR, lw=1.6, ms=12)
    ax.text(xv + 1.25 * n, 0.0, "$n=%+d$" % n, ha="left" if n > 0 else "right",
            va="center", fontsize=12, color=REACTCLR)
ax.text(Ld / 2, -0.95,
        r"$\Omega = \, ]0, L[ \qquad \bar\Omega = [0, L] \qquad "
        r"\Gamma = \{0, L\} = \Gamma_g \cup \Gamma_h$",
        ha="center", va="top", fontsize=13)
tidy(ax)
ax.set_xlim(-2.9, Ld + 2.9)
ax.set_ylim(-1.55, 0.85)
fig_domain_path = save(fig, "R_Fig2_Domain.png")
```

![The same domain as for the wall: the open interval $\Omega$, its two end points
$\Gamma$, and the outward unit normal at each.](`{python} fig_domain_path`){#fig-r-domain width=78%}

::: {.step .notes}
- $\Omega = \,]0, L[$ is the inside of the rod; $\bar\Omega = [0, L]$ adds its two ends.
- $\Gamma = \{0, L\}$, with outward normals $n = -1$ at $x = 0$ and $n = +1$ at $x = L$.
- Each end gets exactly one condition: its **displacement** is known, or the **force on
  it** is known. $\Gamma = \Gamma_g \cup \Gamma_h$, $\Gamma_g \cap \Gamma_h = \emptyset$.
:::

## The quantities and their units

| Symbol | Meaning | SI units | This example |
|---|---|---|---|
| $x$ | position along the axis | m | $0 \le x \le L$, down the pile |
| $L$ | length | m | 10 m |
| $u(x)$ | axial displacement, positive toward $+x$ | m (report in mm) | unknown |
| $\varepsilon = u_{,x}$ | axial strain | m/m (dimensionless) | unknown |
| $\sigma = E\varepsilon$ | axial stress, tension positive | Pa (MPa) | unknown |
| $E$ | Young's modulus | Pa (GPa) | 30 GPa, concrete |
| $A$ | cross-sectional area | m² | 0.09 m² (300 × 300 mm) |
| $K = EA$ | axial stiffness | N | $2.7\times10^{9}$ N |
| $N = EA\,u_{,x}$ | internal axial force, tension positive | N (kN) | unknown |
| $f(x)$ | distributed axial load per unit length, positive toward $+x$ | N/m (kN/m) | −40 kN/m |
| $g$ | prescribed end displacement | m | 0 |
| $h$ | prescribed end force, positive toward $+x$ | N (kN) | +900 kN |

::: {.step}
Hughes' elasticity chapter writes the same problem **per unit area**: $\sigma_{,x} + b = 0$,
with a body force $b$ in N/m³ and a traction $h$ in Pa. For a rod of constant $A$, multiply
through by $A$: $f = bA$ in N/m, and $h$ becomes a force in N. The pictures are the same.
:::

## Where the differential equation comes from

### Kinematics: displacement and strain

```{python fig_kinematics}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

Lk, K = 6.0, 1.0
fk, hk = 0.10, 0.25
uk = lambda x: (hk + fk * Lk) * x / K - fk * x ** 2 / (2 * K)
xs = np.linspace(0, Lk, 7)
exag = 1.0

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8.4, 6.2),
                         gridspec_kw=dict(height_ratios=[1.0, 1.25]))
ax = axes[0]
y0, y1 = 1.5, 0.0
box(ax, 0, Lk, y0 - 0.2, y0 + 0.2, fc=ROD)
box(ax, 0, Lk + uk(Lk), y1 - 0.2, y1 + 0.2, fc="#f3d6d0", ec=INK)
hatch_wall(ax, 0, y1 - 0.5, y0 + 0.5, side=-1, n=9, size=0.25)
for i, xv in enumerate(xs):
    xd = xv + uk(xv)
    ax.plot([xv, xv], [y0 - 0.2, y0 + 0.2], color=INK, lw=1.4, zorder=3)
    ax.plot([xd, xd], [y1 - 0.2, y1 + 0.2], color=INK, lw=1.4, zorder=3)
    ax.plot([xv, xd], [y0 - 0.2, y1 + 0.2], color=DIMCLR, lw=0.8, ls=":")
    ax.text(xv + (0.12 if i == 0 else 0), y0 + 0.28, "$x_{%d}$" % i,
            ha="left" if i == 0 else "center", va="bottom", fontsize=10.5)
i = 4
arrow(ax, (xs[i], y1 - 0.36), (xs[i] + uk(xs[i]), y1 - 0.36), color=LOADCLR,
      lw=1.6, ms=11)
ax.text(xs[i] + uk(xs[i]) / 2, y1 - 0.45, "$u(x_4)$", ha="center", va="top",
        fontsize=11, color=LOADCLR)
arrow(ax, (Lk + uk(Lk), y1), (Lk + uk(Lk) + 0.9, y1), color=LOADCLR, lw=2.2,
      ms=14)
ax.text(Lk + 0.25, y0, "before", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=10.5,
        color=DIMCLR)
ax.text(Lk + uk(Lk) + 1.0, y1 + 0.32, "after", ha="left", va="bottom",
        fontsize=10.5, color=DIMCLR)
tidy(ax)
ax.set_xlim(-0.6, Lk + uk(Lk) + 1.8)
ax.set_ylim(-1.0, 2.2)

ax = axes[1]
xx = np.linspace(0, Lk, 200)
ax.plot(xx, uk(xx), color=LOADCLR, lw=2.4)
ax.plot(xs, uk(xs), "o", color=LOADCLR, ms=6)
x0, run = 2.0, 1.2
s = (hk + fk * Lk) / K - fk * x0 / K
ax.plot([x0, x0 + run, x0 + run], [uk(x0), uk(x0), uk(x0) + s * run],
        color=INK, lw=1.2)
ax.plot([x0 - 0.8, x0 + run + 0.4], [uk(x0) - 0.8 * s, uk(x0) + (run + 0.4) * s],
        color=INK, lw=1.2, ls="--")
ax.text(x0 + run / 2, uk(x0) - 0.05, r"$\Delta x$", ha="center", va="top",
        fontsize=11)
ax.text(x0 + run + 0.08, uk(x0) + s * run / 2, r"$\Delta u$", ha="left",
        va="center", fontsize=11)
ax.text(x0 + run + 0.6, uk(x0) + s * (run + 0.4) - 0.05,
        r"strain $\varepsilon = \lim\ \Delta u / \Delta x = u_{,x}$",
        ha="left", va="top", fontsize=11.5)
ax.set_xticks(xs)
ax.set_xticklabels(["$x_{%d}$" % i for i in range(len(xs))])
ax.set_yticks([])
ax.set_xlim(-0.1, Lk + 0.1)
graph(ax, "$x$", "displacement $u(x)$")
fig.tight_layout(h_pad=0.6)
fig_kin_path = save(fig, "R_Fig3_Kinematics.png")
```

![Top: a rod before and after loading (displacements greatly exaggerated). Each material
point $x_i$ moves to $x_i + u(x_i)$. Bottom: the same displacements as a function. Where
the curve is steep, neighbouring points separate fast — the rod is stretched
there.](`{python} fig_kin_path`){#fig-r-kinematics width=84%}

The **displacement** $u(x)$ is how far the material point that started at $x$ has moved
along the axis. Two neighbouring points $\Delta x$ apart end up $\Delta x + \Delta u$
apart, so the **strain** — change in length per unit length — is the slope of the
displacement:

::: {.derivation}
$$
\varepsilon = \lim_{\Delta x \to 0} \frac{\left(\Delta x + \Delta u\right) - \Delta x}{\Delta x}
= u_{,x}
\qquad\qquad
u_{,x} > 0 \;\text{stretched (tension)}, \qquad u_{,x} < 0 \;\text{shortened (compression)}
$$
:::

::: {.step}
A **uniform** shift of the whole rod, $u = $ constant, has $u_{,x} = 0$: it moves the rod
without straining it. Hold on to this; it is why a rod with no support is not a solvable
problem.
:::

### Material: Hooke's law, from stress to force

```{python fig_hooke}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

fig, (ax, bx) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9.6, 3.4),
                             gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[1.0, 1.35]))
eps = np.linspace(0, 0.0012, 50)
ax.plot(eps * 1e3, 30e9 * eps / 1e6, color=INK, lw=2.4)
ax.plot([0.4, 0.8, 0.8], [12, 12, 24], color=LOADCLR, lw=1.2)
ax.text(0.82, 18, "$E$", color=LOADCLR, fontsize=13, va="center")
ax.text(0.05, 33, r"$\sigma = E\,\varepsilon$", fontsize=13, va="top")
ax.set_xlim(0, 1.25)
ax.set_ylim(0, 37)
graph(ax, r"strain $\varepsilon$ (×10⁻³)", r"stress $\sigma$ (MPa)")
ax.set_title("linear elastic material ($E$ = 30 GPa)", fontsize=11)

# a rod cut open: stress spread over the section adds up to N
box(bx, 0, 3.0, -0.8, 0.8, fc=ROD)
bx.add_patch(Ellipse((3.0, 0), 0.5, 1.6, facecolor="#cfcfcf", edgecolor=INK,
                     lw=1.3, zorder=2))
for yv in np.linspace(-0.62, 0.62, 7):
    arrow(bx, (3.0 + 0.1 * math.sqrt(max(0, 1 - (yv / 0.8) ** 2)), yv),
          (3.75, yv), color=LOADCLR, lw=1.1, ms=8)
bx.text(3.85, 0.95, r"$\sigma$ on each bit of $A$", ha="left", va="bottom",
        fontsize=10.5, color=LOADCLR)
arrow(bx, (4.75, 0), (6.1, 0), color=REACTCLR, lw=2.8, ms=17)
bx.text(5.45, -0.25, r"$N = \sigma A = EA\,u_{,x}$", ha="center", va="top",
        fontsize=12.5, color=REACTCLR)
bx.text(4.4, 0.0, "=", fontsize=16, ha="center", va="center")
bx.text(1.5, 0, "$A$", fontsize=13, ha="center", va="center")
tidy(bx)
bx.set_xlim(-0.2, 6.4)
bx.set_ylim(-1.4, 1.5)
fig.tight_layout(w_pad=2.5)
fig_hooke_path = save(fig, "R_Fig4_Hooke.png")
```

![Left: a linear elastic material, $\sigma = E\varepsilon$. Right: the stress on a cut,
added up over the cross-section, is the internal axial force $N$ — drawn here in
tension, pulling outward on the cut face.](`{python} fig_hooke_path`){#fig-r-hooke width=90%}

::: {.derivation}
$$
N = \sigma A = E A\,\varepsilon = EA\,u_{,x}
\qquad\qquad [\text{Pa}\cdot\text{m}^2 = \text{N}]
$$
:::

This is the rod's version of Fourier's law, with one sign difference: here there is **no
minus sign**. Heat flows *down* the temperature gradient, but a rod pulls back *along*
its stretch.

```{python fig_slice}
fig_slice_path = save(fig, "R_Fig5_Slice.png")
```

![Free body of a slice of length $\Delta x$. The rest of the rod pulls on each face with
the internal force $N$; the distributed load contributes $f\,\Delta x$.](`{python} fig_slice_path`){#fig-r-slice width=80%}

Sum the forces in $+x$. The rod to the left pulls the slice toward $-x$ with $N(x)$; the
rod to the right pulls it toward $+x$ with $N(x+\Delta x)$:

::: {.derivation}
$$
-N(x) + N(x + \Delta x) + f\,\Delta x = 0
\qquad\xrightarrow[\;\text{divide by } \Delta x,\; \Delta x \to 0\;]{}\qquad
N_{,x} + f = 0
$$
:::

::: {.step}
Read it as **"the internal force drops by exactly the load applied along the way"**:
$N_{,x} = -f$. In the pile, friction pushes up ($f < 0$), so $N$ grows toward
$+x$. The compression is largest at the head and the soil takes some of it off as you
go down.
:::

Substituting $N = EA\,u_{,x}$ gives the differential equation of the strong form:

::: {.derivation}
$$
-\left(EA\,u_{,x}\right)_{,x} = f
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\left(EA\,u_{,x}\right)_{,x} + f = 0
\quad\xrightarrow{\;EA \text{ constant}\;}\quad
EA\,u_{,xx} + f = 0
\quad\xrightarrow{\;EA = 1\;}\quad
u_{,xx} + f = 0 \;\;\text{(Hughes)}
$$
:::

### What the equation says about the shape of $u$

```{python fig_curvature}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 4.3))
xx = np.linspace(0, L, 200)
u0, uL = 0.0, 1.0e-3
for fv, col, lab in ((+100e3, LOADCLR, "$f$ = +100 kN/m (toward $+x$): concave down"),
                     (0, INK, "$f = 0$: straight line (uniform strain)"),
                     (-100e3, REACTCLR, "$f$ = −100 kN/m (toward $-x$): concave up")):
    u = u0 + (uL - u0) * xx / L + fv / (2 * EA) * xx * (L - xx)
    ax.plot(xx, u * 1e3, color=col, lw=2.2, label=lab)
for xv, uv in ((0, u0), (L, uL)):
    ax.plot([xv], [uv * 1e3], "o", color=BDRYCLR, ms=8, zorder=5)
ax.text(-0.3, 0.0, "$u(0)$ = 0", color=BDRYCLR, fontsize=10.5, ha="right",
        va="center")
ax.text(L + 0.3, 1.0, "$u(L)$ = 1 mm", color=BDRYCLR, fontsize=10.5,
        ha="left", va="center")
ax.set_xlim(-2.6, L + 2.9)
ax.set_xticks(range(0, 11, 2))
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=10.5, loc="upper center",
          bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.2))
graph(ax, "$x$ (m)", "$u$ (mm)")
fig_curv_path = save(fig, "R_Fig6_Curvature.png")
```

![Three rods with the same end displacements and different distributed loads
($EA = 2.7\times10^9$ N, $L$ = 10 m). With no load the displacement is linear and the strain
is the same everywhere; a load bows it.](`{python} fig_curv_path`){#fig-r-curvature width=74%}

::: {.step .notes}
- $u_{,xx} = -f/EA$: the load sets the **curvature** of the displacement, just as heat
  generation set the curvature of the temperature.
- $f = 0$: $u$ is linear, $\varepsilon$ and $N$ are constant — the familiar
  $\delta = PL/EA$ bar.
- $f \ne 0$: the strain, and therefore $N$, changes along the rod at the rate $-f$.
:::

## The forcing function $f$

$f(x)$ is an axial load **per unit length** of rod, in N/m, positive when it points
toward $+x$. It is the only data that acts in the interior of $\Omega$. Integrated over
the length, it is the total distributed force, in N:

::: {.derivation}
$$
\int_0^L f\,dx \quad \left[\tfrac{\text{N}}{\text{m}}\cdot\text{m} = \text{N}\right]
\qquad\text{e.g.}\qquad (-40\ \text{kN/m})(10\ \text{m}) = -400\ \text{kN}
\quad\text{(400 kN carried by friction, upward)}
$$
:::

```{python fig_forcing}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
```

![Three distributed axial loads. Arrow length is proportional to $|f|$, and the sign of
$f$ is read against the $x$ arrow drawn in each panel.](`{python} fig_forcing_path`){#fig-r-forcing width=98%}

::: {.step .notes}
- **Self-weight** of a vertical member: $f = \rho g A$. It is often negligible — 38.5 N/m
  for a 500 mm² steel rod — but not for long hoist cables or tall columns.
- **Skin friction** along a pile or ground anchor: the soil resists the motion, so $f$
  points opposite to the motion.
- **Inertial (centrifugal) load** on a spinning member: $f = \rho A\omega^2 x$, which
  grows with distance from the hub.
- Loads that act at a **point** (a bracket bolted halfway along) are not an $f$ in the
  strong form: $f$ would have to be a delta function, and $u_{,xx}$ would not exist
  there. The weak form handles them naturally; the strong form does not.
:::

## Boundary conditions

Each end gets exactly one condition: either its **displacement** is known, or the
**force applied to it** is known. Never both, and never neither.

### Dirichlet: $u = g$ on $\Gamma_g$ — the displacement is known

```{python fig_dirichlet}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

fig, (ax, bx) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10.0, 2.8))
# a rigid support: g = 0
box(ax, 0, 4.0, -0.25, 0.25)
hatch_wall(ax, 4.0, -0.8, 0.8, side=1, n=7, size=0.3)
ax.plot([4.0], [0], "o", color=BDRYCLR, ms=9, zorder=7)

        color=DIMCLR)

ax.set_xlim(-0.5, 5.3)
```

![Two Dirichlet conditions. Left: a support that does not move. Right: an end driven a
known distance, drawn exaggerated; the dashed outline is where the rod was.](`{python} fig_dir_path`){#fig-r-dirichlet width=96%}

::: {.step .notes}
- $g$ is a **displacement**, in m. $g = 0$ is the ordinary fixed support.
- A Dirichlet condition pins the *value* of $u$ and says nothing about the slope, and so
  nothing about the force there. The force the support supplies — the **reaction** — is
  an output, found after solving: $N$ at that end.
- It is an **essential** boundary condition. In the weak form, it is built into the trial
  space $\mathcal{S}$.
:::

### Neumann: $(EA\,u_{,x})\,n = h$ on $\Gamma_h$ — the end force is known {#sec-rod-neumann}

At an end with no support, the only thing holding the rod in equilibrium is the applied
force. Take a sliver of rod right at the end. The applied force $h$ acts on its outer
face, and the rest of the rod pulls on its inner face with $N$, toward the inside:

::: {.derivation}
$$
\text{at } x = L:\quad h - N(L) = 0
\qquad\qquad
\text{at } x = 0:\quad h + N(0) = 0
$$
:::

Both are one statement, $N\,n = h$. With $N = EA\,u_{,x}$, that is exactly the Neumann
condition of the strong form:

::: {.derivation}
$$
h = \sigma A\, n = \left(EA\,u_{,x}\right) n
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
\text{at } x = 0:\; -EA\,u_{,x}(0) = h
\qquad\qquad
\text{at } x = L:\; +EA\,u_{,x}(L) = h
$$
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## $h$ means something different here than for the wall

For the **rod**, $h = \sigma A\,n$ is the $x$-component of the applied **force vector**:
$h > 0$ means the force points toward $+x$, **whichever end** it acts on. So $h > 0$
**pushes** on the left end (compression) but **pulls** on the right end (tension).

For the **wall**, $h = -q\,n$ is the heat flux **into** the body: $h > 0$ means heat
enters, whichever face it acts on.

The equations $\mp K u_{,x} = h$ are identical, so the *slopes* in the two problems
behave identically. What changes is which way the arrow in the picture points.
:::

```{python fig_neumann}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(10.4, 6.4))
W = 2.2
titles = ["$h > 0$: force toward $+x$", "$h = 0$: free end",
          "$h < 0$: force toward $-x$"]
for i, side in enumerate(("left", "right")):
    inside = +1 if side == "left" else -1
    for j, hs in enumerate((+1, 0, -1)):
        ax = axes[i, j]
        push = hs * inside > 0
        state = "stress-free" if hs == 0 else ("compression" if push else "tension")
        # the displacement near the end, above the rod
        slope = (-hs if side == "left" else hs) * 0.45
        xs = np.linspace(0, inside * W, 50)
        ax.plot(xs, 0.75 + slope * xs - 0.04 * xs ** 2, color=INK, lw=2.2,
                zorder=4)
        tt = np.array([0, inside * 1.4])
        ax.plot(tt, 0.75 + slope * tt, color=LOADCLR, lw=1.3, ls="--",
                zorder=4)
        ax.plot([0], [0.75], "o", color=INK, ms=5, zorder=5)
        ax.text(inside * W, 0.75 + slope * inside * W - 0.04 * W ** 2 + 0.22,
                "$u$", fontsize=11, ha="right" if inside > 0 else "left")
        ax.plot([0, 0], [-1.5, 1.95], color=DIMCLR, lw=0.8, ls=":")
        # the rod itself, coloured by what the end force does to it
        fc = {"tension": "#f3d6d0", "compression": "#d6e2f3",
              "stress-free": ROD}[state]
        box(ax, 0, inside * W, -1.15, -0.65, fc=fc, lw=1.2)
        ax.text(inside * W / 2, -0.9, state, ha="center", va="center",
                fontsize=10)
        yA = -0.9
        if hs != 0:
            far = -inside * 1.35
            p0, p1 = ((far, yA), (0, yA)) if push else ((0, yA), (far, yA))
            arrow(ax, p0, p1, color=LOADCLR, lw=2.6, ms=16)
            ax.text(far / 2, yA + 0.2, "push" if push else "pull",
                    color=LOADCLR, fontsize=11, ha="center", va="bottom")
        else:
            ax.text(-inside * 0.7, yA, "nothing\napplied", color=DIMCLR,
                    fontsize=9.5, ha="center", va="center")
        if side == "left":
            rel = {1: "< 0", 0: "= 0", -1: "> 0"}[hs]
            eq = r"$-EA\,u_{,x}(0) = h \;\Rightarrow\; u_{,x}(0) %s$" % rel
        else:
            rel = {1: "> 0", 0: "= 0", -1: "< 0"}[hs]
            eq = r"$EA\,u_{,x}(L) = h \;\Rightarrow\; u_{,x}(L) %s$" % rel
        ax.text(0, -1.55, eq, ha="center", va="top", fontsize=11)
        if i == 0:
            ax.set_title(titles[j], fontsize=12, pad=10)
        ax.set_xlim(-2.4, 2.4)
        ax.set_ylim(-2.1, 2.0)
        tidy(ax)
fig.text(0.005, 0.74, "left end\n$x = 0$\n$n = -1$", ha="left", va="center",
         fontsize=11.5)
fig.text(0.005, 0.27, "right end\n$x = L$\n$n = +1$", ha="left", va="center",
         fontsize=11.5)
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.09, right=0.99, wspace=0.08, hspace=0.18)
fig_neu_path = save(fig, "R_Fig9_Neumann.png")
```

![The Neumann condition at either end of a rod. The black curve is the displacement near
the end and the dashed red line its tangent — the strain there. Compare row by row with the
same figure for the wall: the slopes are identical, but for the rod a positive $h$ always
points toward $+x$, so on the right end it pulls, where for the wall it pushed heat
in.](`{python} fig_neu_path`){#fig-r-neumann width=100%}

::: {.step .notes}
- $h$ is a **force**, in N, positive toward $+x$ (or, per unit area, a traction in Pa).
- $h = 0$ is a **free end**: no force, so zero strain — the displacement curve arrives
  flat.
- The **magnitude** of the slope is $|h|/EA$. For the pile, $900\ \text{kN} / 2.7\times10^9\
  \text{N} = 3.33\times10^{-4}$: the head is shortened by 0.33 mm per metre.
- It is a **natural** boundary condition. In the weak form it appears as the boundary term
  $w(0)\,h$.
- A spring support, $h = -k_s\,u$, mixes value and slope. That is a Robin condition and is
  not part of the model problem.
:::

### Which end gets which condition

```{python fig_configs}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

xx = np.linspace(0, L, 200)
K = EA
configs = [
    ("(a)  Hughes: $\\Gamma_h = \\{0\\}$, $\\Gamma_g = \\{L\\}$ — the pile",
     ("h", P), ("g", 0.0), fsk,
     0.0 + P / K * (L - xx) + fsk / (2 * K) * (L ** 2 - xx ** 2)),
    ("(b)  swapped: $\\Gamma_g = \\{0\\}$, $\\Gamma_h = \\{L\\}$ — the pile, mirrored",
     ("g", 0.0), ("h", -P), -fsk,
     0.0 + (-P + (-fsk) * L) / K * xx - (-fsk) / (2 * K) * xx ** 2),
    ("(c)  both Dirichlet: $\\Gamma_g = \\{0, L\\}$, $\\Gamma_h = \\emptyset$",
     ("g", 2.0e-3), ("g", 0.0), fsk,
     2.0e-3 * (1 - xx / L) + fsk / (2 * K) * xx * (L - xx)),
    ("(d)  both Neumann: $\\Gamma_h = \\{0, L\\}$, $\\Gamma_g = \\emptyset$",
     ("h", P), ("h", -(P + fsk * L)), fsk, None),
]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 2, figsize=(10.0, 11.0),
                         gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[1.0, 1.25]))
for i, (title, bcL, bcR, fv, u) in enumerate(configs):
    ax = axes[i, 0]
    box(ax, 0, 3.0, -0.22, 0.22, fc="#d9d9d9")
    axial_arrows(ax, 0, 3.0, 0.45, np.sign(fv), n=6, size=0.35,
                 color=REACTCLR if fv < 0 else LOADCLR)
    ax.text(1.5, -0.4, ("$f$ = %+.0f kN/m" % (fv / 1e3)).replace("-", "−"),
            ha="center", va="top", fontsize=10,
            color=REACTCLR if fv < 0 else LOADCLR)
    for xv, (kind, val), inside in ((0.0, bcL, +1), (3.0, bcR, -1)):
        if kind == "g":
            hatch_wall(ax, xv, -0.55, 0.55, side=-inside, n=5, size=0.22)
            ax.text(xv - inside * 0.25, 0.75, "$g$ = %.0f mm" % (val * 1e3),
                    ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=10.5, color=BDRYCLR)
        else:
            push = np.sign(val) * inside > 0
            far = xv - inside * 1.2
            p0, p1 = ((far, 0), (xv, 0)) if push else ((xv, 0), (far, 0))
            arrow(ax, p0, p1, color=LOADCLR, lw=2.4, ms=15)
            ax.text(xv - inside * 0.6, 0.35,
                    ("$h$ = %+.0f\nkN" % (val / 1e3)).replace("-", "−"),
                    ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=10.5, color=LOADCLR)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=11, loc="left")
    tidy(ax)
    ax.set_xlim(-1.6, 4.6)
    ax.set_ylim(-1.1, 1.6)

    ax = axes[i, 1]
    ax.axhline(0, color=DIMCLR, lw=0.7)
    if u is not None:
        ax.plot(xx, u * 1e3, color=INK, lw=2.2)
        for xv, (kind, val), inside in ((0.0, bcL, +1), (L, bcR, -1)):
            ui = np.interp(xv, xx, u) * 1e3
            if kind == "g":
                ax.plot([xv], [ui], "o", color=BDRYCLR, ms=8, zorder=5)
            else:
                s = (val / K) * (-1 if xv == 0 else 1) * 1e3
                tt = np.array([xv, xv + inside * 3.0])
                ax.plot(tt, ui + s * (tt - xv), color=LOADCLR, lw=2.0, ls="--")
    else:
        base = -P / K * xx - fsk / (2 * K) * xx ** 2
        for c in (1.0e-3, 2.0e-3, 3.0e-3, 4.0e-3):
            ax.plot(xx, (c + base) * 1e3, color=INK if c == 3.0e-3 else "0.6",
                    lw=2.2 if c == 3.0e-3 else 1.3,
                    ls="-" if c == 3.0e-3 else "--")
        ax.text(0.5 * L, 4.2, "$u + C$ solves it for every constant $C$:\n"
                "the pile can float up or down as a rigid body",
                ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xlim(-0.2, L + 0.2)
    ax.set_ylim(-3.2, 5.4)
    graph(ax, "$x$ (m)" if i == 3 else None, "$u$ (mm)")
fig.tight_layout(h_pad=1.4, w_pad=2.0)
fig_configs_path = save(fig, "R_Fig10_Configurations.png")
```

::: {.step .notes}
- **(a) Hughes' arrangement.** Force given at $x = 0$, displacement at $x = L$:
  $\;u(L) = g,\;\; -EA\,u_{,x}(0) = h$. This is the pile: 900 kN pushing down (toward
  $+x$) on the head, the toe fixed on rock.
- **(b) Swapped.** Displacement given at $x = 0$, force at $x = L$:
  $\;u(0) = g,\;\; +EA\,u_{,x}(L) = h$. Drawn here as the **mirror image** of (a) — the
  same pile, stood on its head. Because $x$ now runs from the toe to the head, the column
  load points toward $-x$ and **$h$ = −900 kN**; the friction flips too, $f$ = +40 kN/m.
  Compare the wall, where the mirror image kept $h$ = +50 W/m². A force has a direction
  in space; a heat inflow does not.
- **(c) Two Dirichlet ends** is well-posed: here the head is jacked down 2 mm and the toe
  is fixed. The curve is a straight line plus the small bow from the friction.
- **(d) Two Neumann ends** is **not** well-posed:
    - *Uniqueness fails.* Force data see only $u_{,x}$, so any rigid-body shift
      $u + C$ is also a solution. Nothing stops the pile from floating.
    - *Existence needs equilibrium.* The applied forces must balance:
      $h_0 + h_L + \int_0^L f\,dx = 0$. The panel uses $h_L$ = −500 kN — the rock's
      reaction, handed in as data — so that $900 - 500 - 400 = 0$. Any other $h_L$ and the
      rod accelerates, and there is no static solution.
- So **$\Gamma_g$ must not be empty**: at least one end must be held.
:::

## The strong form, complete

For Hughes' arrangement (a):

::: {.derivation}
$$
(\mathrm{S}) \qquad
\begin{aligned}
&\text{Given } f : \bar\Omega \to \RR \;[\text{N/m}],\;
  EA > 0 \;[\text{N}],\;
  g \;[\text{m}], \text{ and } h \;[\text{N}],
  \text{ find } u : \bar\Omega \to \RR \;[\text{m}] \text{ such that} \\[3pt]
&\qquad \left(EA\,u_{,x}\right)_{,x} + f = 0
   && \text{on } \Omega = \,]0, L[ && \text{(equilibrium + Hooke)} \\
&\qquad u(L) = g && && \text{(Dirichlet: known displacement)} \\
&\qquad -EA\,u_{,x}(0) = h && && \text{(Neumann: known end force)}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

and, for the swapped arrangement (b), $u(0) = g$ and $+EA\,u_{,x}(L) = h$.

::: {.step .notes}
- **Strong** because the equation must hold at every point, which demands $u_{,xx}$
  everywhere. A rod whose area steps from one size to another, or a point load partway
  along, already breaks this; the weak form will not mind.
- With constant $EA$ and $f$, the exact solution of (a) is
:::

::: {.derivation}
$$
u(x) = g + \frac{h}{EA}\,(L - x) + \frac{f}{2EA}\,\left(L^2 - x^2\right)
\qquad\qquad
N(x) = EA\,u_{,x} = -h - f\,x
$$
:::

## Worked example: the pile

```{python example_numbers}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

xx = np.linspace(0, L, 300)
u_a = lambda x: P / EA * (L - x) + fsk / (2 * EA) * (L ** 2 - x ** 2)
N_a = lambda x: -P - fsk * x
u0 = u_a(0.0)
eps0 = -P / EA
```

The pile of @fig-r-pile: $L$ = 10 m, $E$ = 30 GPa, $A$ = 0.09 m², so
$EA = 2.7\times10^{9}$ N. A column pushes down on the head with 900 kN ($h$ = +900 kN,
toward $+x$); skin friction of 40 kN/m acts upward ($f$ = −40 kN/m); the toe sits on
rock ($g$ = 0).

```{python example_math}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

print(r"""
::: {.derivation}
$$
\begin{aligned}
u(x) &= \frac{900\times10^{3}}{2.7\times10^{9}}\,(10 - x)
  + \frac{-40\times10^{3}}{2(2.7\times10^{9})}\,(100 - x^2) \quad [\text{m}] \\[4pt]
u(0) &= %.3f - %.3f = %.2f\ \text{mm (the head settles)}
  \qquad\qquad u_{,x}(0) = -\frac{h}{EA} = %.3f\times10^{-4} \\[4pt]
N(x) &= EA\,u_{,x} = -900 + 40\,x \quad [\text{kN}]
  \qquad\qquad N(0) = -900\ \text{kN}, \quad N(L) = %.0f\ \text{kN}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
""" % (P * L / EA * 1e3, -fsk * L ** 2 / (2 * EA) * 1e3, u0 * 1e3,
       eps0 * 1e4, N_a(L) / 1e3))
```

```{python fig_example}
        va="top", fontsize=10.5, color=REACTCLR)
ax.text(L - 0.15, N_a(L) / 1e3 + 40, "$N(L)$ = −500 kN\n(delivered to rock)",
        ha="right", va="bottom", fontsize=10.5, color=REACTCLR)
ax.text(5.0, -250, "slope $N_{,x} = -f$ = +40 kN/m:\n400 kN shed to the soil by friction",
        ha="center", va="center", fontsize=10.5)
ax.set_ylim(-1150, 60)
graph(ax, "$x$ (m, down the pile)", "axial force $N$ (kN)")

```

![The pile's solution. Top: displacement, zero at the rock and leaving the head with the
slope the column load dictates. Bottom: the internal axial force $N = EA\,u_{,x}$, all
compression, decreasing in magnitude as friction takes load into the
soil.](`{python} fig_example_path`){#fig-r-example width=80%}

Every line of the strong form, checked on the picture:

::: {.step .notes}
- **The differential equation.** $EA\,u_{,xx} = -f > 0$: the displacement curve bends
  upward uniformly. Equivalently $N_{,x} = -f$ = +40 kN/m: the force line in the lower
  panel is straight.
- **The Dirichlet condition.** $u = 0$ at the rock.
- **The Neumann condition.** At the head the tangent drops 0.67 mm over 2 m, a slope of
  $-3.33\times10^{-4}$, and $-EA\,u_{,x}(0) = -2.7\times10^{9}\times(-3.33\times10^{-4})
  = 900$ kN $= h$.
- **Equilibrium of the whole pile.** 900 kN down at the head = 400 kN of friction +
  500 kN at the toe. The Dirichlet end's reaction, 500 kN, came *out* of the solution.
:::

## Explore the strong form

The black curve is the exact $u(x)$ for the settings below, with the pile's
$L$ = 10 m. Blue dots are Dirichlet ends; the dashed red line is the strain a Neumann
condition forces on its end. Under the plots, the rod is drawn twice: grey ticks are
material points before loading, and black ticks are the same points after, with the
displacements exaggerated. The band is shaded by the internal force: red for tension,
blue for compression.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof rBC = Inputs.radio(new Map([
  ["(a) Hughes: h at x = 0, g at x = L", "a"],
  ["(b) swapped: g at x = 0, h at x = L", "b"],
  ["(c) g at both ends", "c"]
]), {value: "a", label: "Boundary conditions"})
viewof rF  = Inputs.range([-150, 150],   {value: -40,  step: 5,   label: "f (kN/m, toward +x)"})
viewof rH  = Inputs.range([-1500, 1500], {value: 900,  step: 25,  label: "h (kN, toward +x)"})
viewof rG  = Inputs.range([-3, 3],       {value: 0,    step: 0.1, label: "g (mm)"})
viewof rG0 = Inputs.range([-3, 3],       {value: 2,    step: 0.1, label: "g at x = 0 in (c) (mm)"})
viewof rEA = Inputs.range([0.5, 10],     {value: 2.7,  step: 0.1, label: "EA (×10⁹ N)"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
rod = {
  const L = 10, K = rEA * 1e9, f = rF * 1e3, h = rH * 1e3, g = rG / 1e3, g0 = rG0 / 1e3;
  let u, du;
  if (rBC === "a") {
    u  = x => g + h / K * (L - x) + f / (2 * K) * (L * L - x * x);
    du = x => -h / K - f * x / K;
  } else if (rBC === "b") {
    u  = x => g + (h + f * L) / K * x - f / (2 * K) * x * x;
    du = x => (h + f * L) / K - f * x / K;
  } else {
    u  = x => g0 + (g - g0) * x / L + f / (2 * K) * x * (L - x);
    du = x => (g - g0) / L + f * (L - 2 * x) / (2 * K);
  }
  const N = x => K * du(x);
  const pts = d3.range(121).map(i => { const x = L * i / 120; return {x, u: 1e3 * u(x), N: N(x) / 1e3}; });
  return {L, K, f, h, u, du, N, pts};
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const {L, u, du, N, pts} = rod;
  const W = Math.min(width, 760);
  const dirX = rBC === "a" ? [L] : rBC === "b" ? [0] : [0, L];
  const neuX = rBC === "a" ? 0 : rBC === "b" ? L : null;
  const marks = [
    Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: "#bbb"}),
    Plot.line(pts, {x: "x", y: "u", stroke: "#1a1a1a", strokeWidth: 2.6}),
    Plot.dot(dirX.map(x => ({x, u: 1e3 * u(x)})), {x: "x", y: "u", r: 6, fill: "#4a7ba7"})
  ];
  if (neuX !== null) {
    const d = (neuX === 0 ? 1 : -1) * 3;
    marks.push(Plot.line([{x: neuX, u: 1e3 * u(neuX)}, {x: neuX + d, u: 1e3 * (u(neuX) + du(neuX) * d)}],
      {x: "x", y: "u", stroke: "#c0392b", strokeWidth: 2.4, strokeDasharray: "7,4"}));
  }
  const top = Plot.plot({
    width: W, height: 280, marginLeft: 55,
    x: {label: "x (m) →", domain: [-0.5, L + 0.5]},
    y: {label: "↑ displacement u (mm)", grid: true},
    marks
  });

  const Nplot = Plot.plot({
    width: W, height: 200, marginLeft: 55,
    x: {label: "x (m) →", domain: [-0.5, L + 0.5]},
    y: {label: "↑ axial force N (kN)", grid: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: "#bbb"}),
      Plot.areaY(pts, {x: "x", y: "N", fill: "#1f6feb", fillOpacity: 0.12}),
      Plot.line(pts, {x: "x", y: "N", stroke: "#1f6feb", strokeWidth: 2.4})
    ]
  });

  // the rod before and after, coloured by N
  const umax = d3.max(pts, p => Math.abs(p.u)) || 1;
  const exag = 0.35 / (umax / 1e3);           // biggest movement drawn as 0.35 m
  const segs = pts.slice(0, -1).map((p, i) => ({x1: p.x + exag * p.u / 1e3,
    x2: pts[i + 1].x + exag * pts[i + 1].u / 1e3, N: p.N}));
  const ticks = d3.range(0, 11).map(i => L * i / 10);
  const Nmax = d3.max(pts, p => Math.abs(p.N)) || 1;
  const band = Plot.plot({
    width: W, height: 130, marginLeft: 55,
    x: {label: `x (m) → — displacements exaggerated ×${exag.toFixed(0)}`, domain: [-0.5, L + 0.5]},
    y: {axis: null, domain: [0, 2]},
    color: {type: "diverging", scheme: "RdBu", reverse: true, domain: [-Nmax, Nmax],
            legend: true, label: "N (kN): red tension, blue compression"},
    marks: [
      Plot.rect([{x1: 0, x2: L}], {x1: "x1", x2: "x2", y1: 1.2, y2: 1.8, fill: "#e2e2e2", stroke: "#999"}),
      Plot.ruleX(ticks, {x: d => d, y1: 1.2, y2: 1.8, stroke: "#888", strokeWidth: 1.5}),
      Plot.rect(segs, {x1: "x1", x2: "x2", y1: 0.2, y2: 0.8, fill: "N", stroke: "N"}),
      Plot.ruleX(ticks, {x: d => d + exag * u(d), y1: 0.2, y2: 0.8, stroke: "#1a1a1a", strokeWidth: 1.5}),
      Plot.link(ticks, {x1: d => d, y1: 1.2, x2: d => d + exag * u(d), y2: 0.8, stroke: "#aaa", strokeDasharray: "2,2"})
    ]
  });
  return html`<div>${top}${Nplot}${band}</div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const {L, K, f, h, u, du, N} = rod;
  const fmt = (v, d = 1) => (v < 0 ? "−" : "") + Math.abs(v).toFixed(d);
  let bc;
  if (rBC === "a") bc = `−EA u,x(0) = ${fmt(-N(0) / 1e3, 0)} kN = h ✓\u2003\u2003u(L) = ${fmt(1e3 * u(L), 2)} mm = g ✓`;
  else if (rBC === "b") bc = `u(0) = ${fmt(1e3 * u(0), 2)} mm = g ✓\u2003\u2003+EA u,x(L) = ${fmt(N(L) / 1e3, 0)} kN = h ✓`;
  else bc = `u(0) = ${fmt(1e3 * u(0), 2)} mm ✓\u2003\u2003u(L) = ${fmt(1e3 * u(L), 2)} mm ✓\u2003\u2003(h is not used: Γₕ = ∅)`;
  // external forces on the rod, toward +x: at x = 0 the force is -N(0), at x = L it is +N(L)
  const F0 = -N(0) / 1e3, FL = N(L) / 1e3, Ff = f * L / 1e3;
  return html`<div style="font-size: 0.95rem; line-height: 1.6; margin: 0.4rem 0 1rem 0;">
    <b>Boundary conditions:</b> ${bc}<br>
    <b>Curvature:</b> u,xx = −f/EA = ${fmt(-f / K * 1e6, 2)} × 10⁻⁶ per m, everywhere<br>
    <b>Equilibrium</b> (forces toward +x): at x = 0: ${fmt(F0, 0)} kN &nbsp;+&nbsp; along the rod ∫f dx: ${fmt(Ff, 0)} kN
    &nbsp;+&nbsp; at x = L: ${fmt(FL, 0)} kN &nbsp;=&nbsp; ${fmt(F0 + Ff + FL, 0)} kN<br>
    <span style="color:#666">Whichever end is Dirichlet, its force above is the support reaction: an output of the solve, not an input.</span>
  </div>`;
}
```

::: {.step .notes}
- In (a), set $h = 0$: a free head. The displacement arrives flat and the whole rod is
  in tension or compression only from friction.
- Switch from (a) to (b) with the same $h$ = +900 kN: the load now **pulls** the far end
  of the rod, the band turns red, and the curve changes shape, not just side. To get the
  mirror image of the pile you must also flip the signs of $h$ and $f$.
- In (a) or (b), double $EA$: every displacement halves, and $N$ does not change at all. The forces are
  set by equilibrium alone; the stiffness only decides how far the rod moves to carry
  them. In (c), where both ends are held, the stiffness does change $N$.
:::
